verses.text: Finally, brothers and sisters, pray for us. Pray that the Lord's message will spread quickly and be honoured, just as it was with you.
And pray that we will be rescued from wicked and evil people, because not everyone has faith.
But the Lord is faithful. He will make you strong and protect you from the evil one.
The Lord gives us confidence about you. We are sure that you are doing what we tell you, and that you will keep on doing it.
May the Lord lead your hearts into God's love and into the patient strength that Christ gives.
Brothers and sisters, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ we command you: keep away from any believer who lives a lazy and disorderly life, and does not follow the teaching we passed on to you.
You know yourselves that you should follow our example. We were not lazy or disorderly when we were with you.
We did not eat anyone's food without paying for it. Instead, we worked hard and struggled night and day, so that we would not be a burden to any of you.
We did this, not because we do not have the right to your help, but to give you an example to follow.
Even when we were with you, we gave you this rule: "Anyone who is not willing to work should not eat."
We hear that some among you are lazy and disorderly. They do not work at all. Instead, they are busy in other people's business.
We command such people, and urge them in the Lord Jesus Christ, to settle down, work quietly and earn their own food.
And as for you, brothers and sisters, never get tired of doing what is right.
If anyone does not obey what we say in this letter, take note of that person. Do not mix with him, so that he will feel ashamed.
But do not treat him as an enemy. Warn him as you would a brother.
Now may the Lord of peace himself give you peace at all times and in every way. The Lord be with all of you.
I, Paul, write this greeting with my own hand. This is the mark in all my letters. This is how I write.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
